speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The international order that underpinned stability and prosperity for over nearly eight decades is breaking down.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The multilateral system that has served us well has weakened.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The rule of law is under strain with the resurgence of a "might is right" approach.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In short, the world has become more contested, more fragmented and ultimately, more dangerous.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Budget 2026 is our action plan to enable Singaporeans to navigate this new reality with confidence and secure our future together.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: A key feature of Budget 2026 was artificial intelligence (AI).

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Budget 2026 aims to harness AI as a strategic advantage and drive national adoption so that Singaporeans can take full advantage of the opportunities afforded by technology.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Budget 2026 also allows us to implement our refreshed economic strategy, continue investing in our workers and drive growth to create jobs, strengthen support for families and advance our social compact, and enhance our security and sustainability.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As we begin this important work, we will take into account the many helpful ideas and suggestions from Members on both sides of the House on what we can do to provide more support for families and couples who aspire to become parents.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is the result of successive Budgets, anchored on fiscal prudence, forward planning and catalysing new ways to catch the winds of change even as we provide for current needs.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is in contrast to many other major economies, where public debt is rising, straining their financial stability and weighing on growth prospects.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: When the surplus was first made known in the Budget Statement, some questioned why the surplus was so large and whether the Government had been too conservative.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Budget Statement was delivered on 12 February, against the backdrop of 5% gross domestic product (GDP) growth, when the world had more or less adjusted to the United States (US) tariffs and things seemed to be getting back on an even keel.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, within the span of just three weeks since the Budget Statement was delivered, the world changed again.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On 20 February, eight days after the Budget Statement, the US Supreme Court struck down President Trump's Liberation Day tariffs.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: President Trump responded by doubling down on tariffs the next day, triggering another round of economic uncertainty.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On 26 February, hostilities between Pakistan and Afghanistan erupted.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On 28 February, the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Iran is retaliating, not just against the US and Israel, but also against other countries in the region, plunging the Middle East into another round of instability.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: No one knows how long the conflict will last.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These developments have added to the overall climate of uncertainty.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The business outlook for trade and investment may have to be adjusted.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If so, there will be implications for business costs and daily costs of living.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As a small and open economy, Singapore will feel the knock-on impacts keenly.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have the ability to do more for Singaporeans with ballast and buffer against potential turbulence.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our approach of fiscal prudence has been validated time and time again.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The global economy was calm, the outlook rosy even.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But within a month, we were plunged into the thick of a pandemic, the crisis of a generation and the global economy shut down.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We ended up delivering another four Budgets and drew down about $40 billion of Past Reserves.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In 2022, the Budget Statement was delivered on 18 February.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At that time, we were just getting out of COVID-19 and things were looking up.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Within six days, the Russia-Ukraine war started, changing the global geopolitical dynamic once again and adding to energy and supply chain issues, accompanied by inflation at levels unseen since the 1970s.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In all our Budgets, we prepare for the best, but we also plan in case of the worst.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: History is a hard taskmaster, and we must not ignore its lessons.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our Reserves and our surpluses are things to be grateful for.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our fiscal approach is enabled by our unique system of Parliamentary democracy, which has served us well and continues to deliver good results for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: During the Committee of Supply debate, I spoke about then-Deputy Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong’s 1988 speech on the infamous Hendrickson affair, where he outlined three different political models.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Not all Members may have been present in the Chamber when I spoke about it.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, it is worth recapping what he said.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, the American system is one of checks and balances.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Its underlying premise is fundamentally one of distrust, with each branch of government constantly checking the others.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Then you have the British system where the Prime Minister and the Cabinet are given a wider range of discretionary powers.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There is a greater premise of trust, which rests on the mandate given to the party with the majority in Parliament.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The unspoken and unwritten expectation is that those in power are individuals who can be relied upon to always act honourably.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It resembles the British system, except, as Mr Goh noted, Singaporeans have gone further and superimposed on our Constitutional framework the ideal of a political leader who is upright, morally beyond reproach, someone people can trust.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We believe that our leaders must be men and women of ability and integrity, committed to the public good.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The world has changed greatly since Mr Goh spoke in this House in 1988.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So have the way both the US and British political systems operate.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But Mr Goh’s observations remain, if anything, just as relevant today.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But even more important are the people who are elected to represent and serve the people and whether they possess the competence, commitment and conscience to fulfil their duties.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If they do, then you do not need as many rules because they can be trusted to do the right thing.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If they do not, we can impose and improve as many laws and rules as we like, but democracy and politics will still go wrong.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This applies to governments as much as it does to oppositions and governments-in-waiting.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is by no means perfect, and we must and will continue to find ways to improve our system.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But we do have something rare and precious.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Even when there were disagreements, we share a common commitment to building a better Singapore.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I am glad that you only had to use them a few times and as the exception, and not the norm.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On behalf of this House, I thank you once again for your able chairmanship.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are also deeply grateful to the Clerk of Parliament, Deputy Clerk and the other Clerks of Parliament, the Parliament Secretariat and staff, interpreters and translators.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Their dedicated efforts and support behind the scenes ensured that our proceedings went smoothly.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I hope that we can express our appreciation for them too.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: For about a third of the Members in this House, this is your first Budget and Committee of Supply debate.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Just to let you know, this is one of the few and rare occasions that the Speaker gets to speak.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Hon Members, the work we undertake in this House has never been more important.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In a world filled with large dramatic developments, sensational revelations and an unending array of twists and turns, it is the careful, meticulous and practical work of government that makes a difference to people every day.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But as Members would know, I am a big advocate of the maxim “Less is More”.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It has, indeed, been an intense two weeks and I want to start by thanking all Members for your contributions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: From my perspective, there were a few highlights in this year’s debate.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Our unity puts us in a good place to face a very challenging future.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And for the first time, this year’s entire Budget and Committee of Supply debate took place within the period of Ramadan.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, I thank our Muslim colleagues who had to work through this period where every Sitting day ended well past the iftar time.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In fact, last evening, Minister Masagos, as he broke fast, took a sip of water and immediately proceeded to make and deliver his speech.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We honour all our Muslim colleagues for your commitment to your public duties.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: As Speaker, I have the rare privilege of listening to all your speeches and perhaps, more able than most to distinguish between form and substance.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Some Members were able to deliver crisp responses and ask succinct clarifications.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Others were, as they say, a little bit “cheong hei”, or long-winded.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: There was also a one-word response by one Minister – no preamble, context or elaboration needed.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: A simple one-word “No” was all that was required.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: For Minister of State Alvin Tan, a five-word reply will do: “Please don’t feed the birds.” We also know who among us can speak fluently in three languages, are poets in the making, can speak slow and can go at great speed.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Though the latter is not encouraged, as it means risking not only the Minister being unable to fully capture your points, but it also places undue stress on our interpreters.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In the course of these Sittings, we also found out Members’ favourite songs and singers – from Bon Jovi to Black Eyed Peas, 郭富城 or Aaron Kwok, Taylor Swift and our very own Benjamin Kheng.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Throughout the Committee of Supply debate, there was only one day where we had an official break.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: On all other days, we persevered without one.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I did this to the extent possible because I wanted as many Members to be able to seek their clarifications before the guillotine time.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It was certainly not to test one’s stamina without the need to go for a bio break.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Some Members also wondered whether my magic “mute the microphone” button was functioning properly – and as quite a few Members found out, it is in good working order.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I hope this would be used very sparingly, going forward, and look to your self-discipline in that regard.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Indeed, there was a Member who realised she had run out of time and stopped her speech without the need for me to turn the mic off.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Parliamentary speeches are not an exercise in word count.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It is not how many words you use or how fast you speak but clarity and importance of your main message.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: This principle is even more crucial for our political office holders, who must use their time, beyond sharing their Ministry’s plans and explaining the rationale behind the policies, also tell Singaporeans how our lives will be improved, the trade-offs to be made and what the country is requiring of us.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister Desmond Lee exemplified this approach, though he also gave us a challenging problem to solve.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: How truly Singaporean to have a mathematics test in the Chamber!

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: As they say, “Never a dull moment in Parliament”.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But the true meaning of debate is not when we agree, but how and why we disagree.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: This is not merely partisan disagreement, but a disagreement about ideas, which we have seen within the same party as well as across party lines.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: This, for me, is a mark of the sanctity and legitimacy of the agreements we come to and the laws we make, as well as the trust we have in each other.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Parliament functions best when we come with sound arguments and good intentions, bringing our diverse experiences and backgrounds to discuss and debate.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: When we remain open to listening without prejudice, when we strive to propose solutions, popular or otherwise, for our people, without pandering or playing to the gallery.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We may not hit on the correct note right from the start, but we try and try again.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: To paraphrase Prime Minister Wong and Deputy Prime Minister Gan – and this applies not just to the problem of our low birthrate – we have not, we will not and we cannot give up.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Each day, we wake up to an increasingly fractured world.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: There will be more debates, more Bills to pass and more challenges ahead.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Before I conclude, let me express my gratitude to the Leader of the House, Minister Indranee Rajah; Deputy Leader, Senior Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad; my two Deputy Speakers, Mr Christopher de Souza and Mr Xie Yao Quan; and also to my dedicated and competent Parliamentary Clerks and all Parliamentary staff, who are unseen but invaluable work ensured that proceedings went smoothly throughout these two weeks.
